How a per-link estimate is built

Method, as implemented in link_latency.py

The controller probes round-trip time per active path, not per link — there is no per-link ping in this testbed. link_latency.py attributes a path's measured RTT equally across the links of that path and smooths each link's share with an EWMA, expiring estimates that go stale. That attribution is an estimate by construction, and this page exposes its fingerprint: when the recorded series for every link are identical, the summary says so, because equal splitting of the same path measurements is exactly what produces identical series.

The estimates feed routing through scorer_candidates(): the multi-objective scorer receives an rtt_ms value per candidate path, summed from the per-link estimates, so a path can win on delay as well as on predicted utilization. Every estimate the controller used is written to latency.csv at probe time — the rows below are those records, aggregated at request time.

For the paper, latency claims must be stated at path level (the measured quantity), with the per-link split described as the attribution method above. This page is the reproducibility surface for that claim and names every source file it was computed from.
